name: billy woods
label: Backwoodz Studioz
lede: A D.C.-born, Zimbabwe-raised rapper who runs his own label, keeps his face out of the pictures, and spent two decades making the densest records in New York before Pitchfork ranked GOLLIWOG No. 21 of 2025.

eras.title: A front-row seat, then a laundromat
eras.text: Born in Washington, D.C., raised for nearly a decade in newly independent Zimbabwe, back in the States at eleven. The rapper who would later hide his face arrives with a Jamaican mother, a Zimbabwean father and a head full of Public Enemy.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · UGSMAG: billy woods · Bandcamp Daily: Billy Woods Raps From the Shadows
years.h: A Jamaican mother, a Zimbabwean father, a D.C. birth
years.p: [[billy woods|f30fea51-fa9c-4067-bc49-fc43236e89ba]] is born in Washington, D.C., to a Jamaican English-literature professor and a Zimbabwean Marxist intellectual who was in the U.S. finishing a Ph.D. during the war for Zimbabwe's independence.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts the birth around 1978. He has never made his birth name public, and he keeps his face out of photos. In 2013 the interviewer MC Eleven, who had known him since 2008, admitted he still had no clear idea what woods looks like.

Bandcamp Daily describes the father as an activist and writer for Zimbabwean independence while exiled in America. In 1980 the family moved to Zimbabwe and he joined the new government, giving woods a front-row seat, he says, to a country still working out its future. His father died in the 1980s; woods and his mother left for the U.S. about eighteen months later, in 1989.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · Bandcamp Daily: Billy Woods Raps From the Shadows
years.h: Back to D.C., and Public Enemy in the headphones
years.p: woods and his mother return to the U.S. He gets into hip-hop through Spike Lee's Do the Right Thing and [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]].
years.xp: He tells Bandcamp Daily he distinctly remembers getting into Public Enemy. He later attends Howard University for a stretch, and a small liberal arts college in the Northeast, before heading for New York.

years.src: Okayplayer: 'The Music Industry Was Detonating Underneath Us · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: He meets Vordul Mega, who tells him to keep writing
years.p: Around age nineteen, woods meets [[Vordul Mega|787c9240-273a-42b3-9163-3ece4c865d71]] of [[Cannibal Ox|38411d0a-5636-46ba-befb-67cca6f4b9c7]] in D.C. The next year, in a laundromat in Kennebunk, Maine, he writes what he calls his first real rhyme.
years.xp: Okayplayer's interview has woods recalling Vordul telling him in 1999 that El-P had signed him; woods says he did not disbelieve it, but was not totally sure. He watched the Cannibal Ox rise from close range, and hearing early versions of tracks like "Pigeons" hit him hard.

eras.title: Wrong decade to start a record label
eras.text: New York, a one-man label and a rap underground that had moved on to Dipset. woods keeps releasing anyway, alone and in crews, for a decade that pays nothing.

years.src: Wikipedia: Backwoodz Studioz · Wikipedia: Vordul Mega · Bandcamp Daily: Billy Woods Raps From the Shadows · Okayplayer: 'The Music Industry Was Detonating Underneath Us
years.h: Camouflage: a solo debut with Vordul on a third of it
years.p: Released through his own new Backwoodz Studioz, it is built on production from 007 (Bond) and later comes to be filed as woods's solo debut.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says he founded Backwoodz Studioz in 2002 as a one-man operation, inspired by indie successes like The Cold Vein and Operation: Doomsday, and rented studio time from Anton Schlesinger, then a Caroline Records intern and later the label's president. Bandcamp Daily says 2003; sources also disagree on whether Camouflage is 2002 or 2003.

He moved to New York for good in 2001, telling Bandcamp Daily he had to escape D.C. before he sat around depressed there forever. Okayplayer has him describing the mid-2000s indie-rap collapse: the same people praising Aesop Rock were suddenly only listening to Dipset. It was, he says, not a great era to start a label in.

years.src: Wikipedia: Vordul Mega · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Terror Firma: ten rappers, one album, mixed notices
years.p: woods joins [[Vordul Mega|787c9240-273a-42b3-9163-3ece4c865d71]], Akir and others from a spread of New York crews for the Reavers album Terror Firma on Backwoodz.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Vordul Mega page says some praised its grit and creativity and others did not warm to it.

years.src: Okayplayer: 'The Music Industry Was Detonating Underneath Us · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Three albums with Privilege as Super Chron Flight Brothers
years.p: Emergency Powers: The World Tour (2007), Indonesia (2009) and Cape Verde (2010) come out with the rapper Privilege.
years.xp: woods tells Okayplayer this was the comedy-and-tragedy period of his output. HipHopDX reviewed Cape Verde in August 2010. The duo broke up in the early 2010s, and Wikipedia says Backwoodz was struggling financially by then.

eras.title: The album that was supposed to be the last one
eras.text: Label broke, group gone, woods plans an exit. Instead the record he thinks of as a goodbye turns him from a cult name into the center of a scene, and he meets the partner who defines the next decade.

years.big: He meant it as the goodbye.
years.src: Wikipedia: History Will Absolve Me · Bandcamp Daily: Backwoodz Studioz · UGSMAG: billy woods
years.h: History Will Absolve Me, made as an exit
years.p: With Super Chron Flight Brothers over and Backwoodz short of money, woods planned this as his final release before leaving the industry.
years.xp:
It did the opposite. Wikipedia calls it a cult classic of underground hip-hop, and Pitchfork later named it the turning point for Backwoodz. Bandcamp Daily's label profile says woods considered it a make-or-break record, and it became the label's first direct-to-fan sale through its own website.

Exclaim! reviewed it in April 2012, and UGSMAG has woods naming "The Man Who Would Be King" and "The Wake" as songs where he finally grasped what he had been chasing for years. Producers he singles out there include Bond, Marmaduke, Willie Green and A.M. Breakups.

years.src: Wikipedia: Armand Hammer (group) · Wikipedia: Backwoodz Studioz
years.h: Elucid, an introduction from Uncommon Nasa, and a new duo
years.p: woods and [[Elucid|1206c904-9282-494d-b9c7-49e8fb201e69]] form [[Armand Hammer|167a6f86-2c26-43fe-82f0-e4c8a39ea490]], named after the industrialist, and release the mixtape Half Measures and the album Race Music.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the two met through the New York rapper Uncommon Nasa, and Elucid signed to Backwoodz around this time. Elucid appears on History Will Absolve Me. Stephen Weil later called Race Music a potent record about life, art, sex, drugs, politics and violence.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · Bandcamp Daily: Backwoodz Studioz
years.h: Dour Candy: a whole album on Blockhead beats
years.p: The New York producer Blockhead makes every beat; Pitchfork's Nate Patrin reviewed it that August, and Noisey's Zachary Lipez called it an invigorating hangover.
years.xp: Blockhead, real name Tony Simon, later released his own Funeral Balloons on Backwoodz. UGSMAG has woods describing it as structurally different from his earlier work.

eras.title: Armand Hammer becomes a name you drop
eras.text: A run of records so consistent the reviews start repeating themselves: Rome, Paraffin, Hiding Places, Shrines. The producer list gets longer, the lyrics get denser, and the label becomes a destination.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Known Unknowns gets a Chekhov comparison
years.p: The Village Voice calls woods the underground rapper Chekhov would listen to; Rolling Stone puts Known Unknowns on a list of 15 great albums you did not hear.
years.xp: Noisey followed in October with a profile arguing woods was at the forefront of rap's avant-garde.

years.src: Wikipedia: Rome (Armand Hammer album)
years.h: Rome: Armand Hammer goes further into the dark
years.p: Messiah Musik, August Fanon, High Priest, Kenny Segal and JPEGMafia are among the producers; Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp: Phillip Mlynar wrote that the duo had burrowed deeper into the leftfield, moving on from boom-bap theology. Paul Thompson at Vulture called it their best. In 2025 Pitchfork placed it at No. 73 on its list of the 100 best rap albums of all time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Paraffin (album)
years.h: Paraffin: vinyl first, then everything else
years.p: Armand Hammer's third album arrives on vinyl from Backwoodz before digital, cassette and CD; Pitchfork's Paul A. Thompson calls it attuned to the political, physical and ethical realities of 2018.
years.xp: Stereogum ranked it fourth among its best rap albums of 2018. It also landed on year-end lists at Pitchfork, the A.V. Club, Bandcamp Daily (No. 28) and PopMatters (No. 65).

years.cap: The William Livingstone House, Detroit, photographed in 2006 by Yves Marchand and Romain Meffre
years.src: Wikipedia: Hiding Places · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Hiding Places: a whole album with Kenny Segal
years.p: The Los Angeles producer, who had already made beats for Armand Hammer's Rome and Paraffin, gets his own full record with woods. Pitchfork gave it 7.7.
years.xp:
Segal came into woods's orbit through Milo's So the Flies Don't Come, which featured Elucid. Pitchfork's Marcus J. Moore heard early-2000s New York underground rap in it and an edginess like Cannibal Ox's The Cold Vein; the Fader called it woods's leanest and best.

It showed up on year-end lists at Time (No. 5), NPR (No. 9), Stereogum (No. 9) and Vice (No. 8). woods also released the solo Terror Management that year, and NPR's Rodney Carmichael put it on a list of Afro-dystopian rap albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shrines (Armand Hammer album)
years.h: Shrines: a song that starts in Edinburgh
years.p: "Bitter Cassava" is begun on a 2019 European tour and finished in New York; guests include Earl Sweatshirt, Moor Mother, Pink Siifu and Quelle Chris.
years.xp: Producers include Earl Sweatshirt, Navy Blue, Nicholas Craven, Child Actor, Andrew Broder and Kenny Segal, with Willie Green as co-executive producer. Pitchfork gave it 8.0; the Quietus's Eden Tizard heard a new clarity after the monolithic Paraffin.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · Wikipedia: Shrines (Armand Hammer album)
years.h: Brass: a full album with Moor Mother
years.p: woods teams up with the Philadelphia poet and musician [[Moor Mother|16610cf1-5ed5-4770-89b4-bf7e7aca7ebf]] for the collaborative Brass.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it as a 2020 collaboration between the two. Moor Mother also appears on Armand Hammer's Shrines and We Buy Diabetic Test Strips.

eras.title: Alchemist, two in one year, Fat Possum
eras.text: The Alchemist produces a full Armand Hammer album, woods releases two solo records in 2022, and Backwoodz signs a distribution deal with Fat Possum.

years.src: Wikipedia: Haram (album) · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Haram: Armand Hammer and the Alchemist
years.p: The Alchemist produces the entire record; Earl Sweatshirt co-produces one track and guests with Quelle Chris and Curly Castro.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 7.8 and later ranked it No. 26 among 2021's best albums. The cover, showing decapitated pigs, drew a PETA statement calling it terrifying and urging people to focus on the music instead.

The Washington Post's Zachary Lipez wrote in March 2021 that the Alchemist made for an even more intriguing brand of underground rap.

years.src: Wikipedia: Aethiopes (album)
years.h: Aethiopes: Preservation produces everything
years.p: The cover borrows Rembrandt's 1661 Two Moors; the title is an old European word for African peoples, and Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp: It topped Treble's year-end list and hit No. 2 at Gorilla vs. Bear, No. 3 at the Ringer and No. 5 at Stereogum. A U.S. tour ran May to October and included Le Guess Who? in the Netherlands in November.

years.src: Wikipedia: Church (billy woods album)
years.h: Church: a second album in one year, built on weed
years.p: The second solo record of 2022 is produced almost entirely by Messiah Musik; Elucid, Akai Solo, Fielded and Fat Ray guest.
years.xp: woods said the album's launching point was cannabis he had not encountered in years, which grew into a record about a certain era in New York, then faith and belief. Pitchfork gave it 7.8 and BrooklynVegan put it at No. 26 for the year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Backwoodz Studioz · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Pitchfork profiles Backwoodz as New York's best underground rap label
years.p: Dylan Green's Pitchfork feature traces how Backwoodz came to be the city's strongest indie rap operation, the same year the label signs a distribution deal with Fat Possum.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the Fat Possum deal to 2023, with Anton Schlesinger as president and woods on A&R and executive production. That year woods also published the children's book A is for Anarchist with the illustrator M. Musgrove (Rizzoli Universe). Armand Hammer's We Buy Diabetic Test Strips came out that September on Fat Possum, their first album outside Backwoodz.

years.src: Wikipedia: Maps (Billy Woods and Kenny Segal album) · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: Maps: 70 percent of it written on tour
years.p: A travelogue with Kenny Segal, featuring Danny Brown, Aesop Rock, Quelle Chris, Benjamin Booker and Samuel T. Herring, gets an 8.9 from Pitchfork.
years.xp:
Written mostly on the road after pandemic restrictions eased and recorded partly in Los Angeles, it is lighter than Hiding Places. Metacritic gave it 90. Pitchfork and Stereogum both ranked it No. 3 of 2023.

NPR's Sheldon Pearce called it a master class, even for one of rap's greatest-ever penmen. Rolling Stone's Mosi Reeves headlined his review with a warning that it is designed to get you lost.

years.src: Wikipedia: We Buy Diabetic Test Strips
years.h: We Buy Diabetic Test Strips: 8.1, and a Fat Possum first
years.p: Armand Hammer's sixth album is produced by El-P, JPEGMAFIA and Kenny Segal, among others, with Shabaka Hutchings and Child Actor in the sessions.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.1; Metacritic scored it 87. BrooklynVegan ranked it No. 2 for the year, Vulture No. 6 and the Ringer No. 7. Guests include JPEGMAFIA, Moor Mother, El-P, Pink Siifu and Soul Glo's Pierce Jordan.

eras.title: GOLLIWOG
eras.text: The most confrontational record of woods's career lands with the biggest reviews of his career. The cover is a golliwog doll, the tracklist is sixteen producers deep, and the year ends with him on a Pitchfork best-of list.

years.src: Wikipedia: Golliwog (album)
years.h: GOLLIWOG announced with "Misery", produced by Kenny Segal
years.p: The lead single is two minutes of Segal beats; "Blk Zmby" follows April 11 and "Lead Paint Test," with Elucid and Cavalier, on May 7.
years.xp: The rollout included a Knockdown Center show in New York. Wikipedia counts it as woods's ninth solo studio album, released again on Backwoodz.

years.src: Wikipedia: Golliwog (album) · Album of the Year: billy woods, GOLLIWOG · Pitchfork: billy woods, GOLLIWOG
years.h: GOLLIWOG: Pitchfork gives it 8.7 and ranks it No. 21 of 2025
years.p: Eighteen tracks in 52 minutes, produced by the Alchemist, El-P, Ant, Conductor Williams, Shabaka Hutchings, DJ Haram, Willie Green and more. The cover is a golliwog doll.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the album's Metacritic score as 88, with 9/10 from Clash, Exclaim! and the Line of Best Fit and 8.7 from Pitchfork; Album of the Year quotes Pitchfork calling it a twisty horrorcore masterpiece where history and nightmares are indistinguishable. The Guardian's Shaad D'Souza found moments of beauty amid the bleakness.

Guests are Elucid (three tracks), Despot, Bruiser Wolf, al.divino, Cavalier and Yolanda Watson. Willie Green mastered all of it and mixed 14 songs. In the UK it reached No. 7 on the R&B chart and No. 26 on the independent chart, and No. 41 in Germany.

years.src: Wikipedia: billy woods · Wikipedia: Golliwog (album)
years.h: The New York Times: "Billy Woods Is Scary Good at Rapping"
years.p: The Times profiles woods six days after GOLLIWOG drops.
years.xp: Wikipedia cites the piece under that headline. The reviews leaned on the same idea: Clash called the record abrasive and demanding, and Slant called it intensely confrontational and unwilling to hold your hand.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mercy (Armand Hammer and the Alchemist album)
years.h: Mercy: Armand Hammer and the Alchemist again
years.p: The duo's second album with the Alchemist, announced September 10, features Earl Sweatshirt, Quelle Chris and Pink Siifu.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Dash Lewis gave it 8.0 and called some of the Alchemist's production his weirdest and most harrowing since The Skeleton Key. Paste ranked it seventh among the best rap albums of 2025.

years.src: Album of the Year: billy woods, GOLLIWOG · Wikipedia: billy woods
years.h: GOLLIWOG lands on the year-end lists: Treble No. 1, the Wire No. 2
years.p: Album of the Year lists Treble at No. 1, the Wire at No. 2 and Rolling Stone's Rob Sheffield at No. 4; Pitchfork puts it at No. 21.
years.xp: Album of the Year has it as the sixth-best-reviewed album of 2025 by its critic average, scored 87 from 21 reviews.
